Timeline::empty_like¶

Back to Timeline API Reference

Signature¶

Timeline Timeline::empty_like() const

Create A Zero-Record Timeline With Compatible Geometry¶

empty_like() creates an empty Timeline whose trailing dimensions and timezone come from the receiver. It is the structural identity for axis-0 operations such as concat(): there are no records yet, but the shape of each future record is already known.

The word “empty” is literal. This method does not allocate uninitialized timestamps with the receiver’s full shape. Temporal values cannot safely expose uninitialized bit patterns as instants. Instead, axis 0 becomes zero:

Receiver shape

Result shape

scalar []

[0]

vector [n]

[0]

matrix [n, d]

[0, d]

array [n, d, e]

[0, d, e]

A scalar therefore becomes an empty one-dimensional sequence. This promotion matches scalar concat() and repeat() behavior: once an operation concerns record count, the scalar is treated as one record.

Values, Timezone, And Ownership¶

No receiver values are read or retained. The result has numel()==0, owns its small empty storage object, and keeps the receiver’s timezone name. Calling the method on a strided timeline is constant in the receiver’s element count because there is no payload to copy.

Example 1. A scalar has no trailing geometry, so its empty counterpart is a length-zero vector.

const auto scalar = pluss::timeline::date("2024-01-01");
std::cout << pluss::timeline::print(scalar.empty_like()) << '\n';

Output¶

Timeline(shape=[0], tz=UTC)[  ]

Example 2. A [2, 1, 2] receiver contributes trailing shape [1, 2]; only the record axis is emptied.

const auto cube = pluss::timeline::date({
    {{"2024-01-01", "2024-01-02"}},
    {{"2024-01-03", "2024-01-04"}},
});
std::cout << pluss::timeline::print(cube.empty_like()) << '\n';

Output¶

Timeline(shape=[0, 1, 2], tz=UTC)

Example 3. The timezone is structural metadata and survives even though no instants remain.

const auto local_empty =
    scalar.tz_convert("America/Edmonton").empty_like();
std::cout << "shape=[" << local_empty.sizes()[0]
          << "] numel=" << local_empty.numel()
          << " tz=" << local_empty.tz() << '\n';

Output¶

shape=[0] numel=0 tz=America/Edmonton

Practical Use¶

Use empty_like() when an algorithm accumulates zero or more compatible temporal blocks and needs a correctly shaped starting value. Do not use it when you need the receiver’s full shape filled with a known instant; that is fill_like(). Do not use it as a placeholder whose elements will later be assigned, because it contains no elements to assign.

The operation has no data-dependent failure mode once the receiver is a valid Timeline. Rank remains within Timeline’s supported scalar-through-3-D range, and changing the leading extent to zero cannot overflow.

See Also¶

  • Timeline::concat: append compatible axis-0 records.

  • Timeline::fill_like: retain the complete shape and fill it.

  • Timeline::repeat: replicate the receiver’s axis-0 block.
